title: Performance Feedback Assertion
description: One optimizer-ready assertion about a media buy, package, or creative. This is a compact projection of buyer- or measurement-provider analysis, not a transport for raw exposure logs, attribution models, or complete study datasets.

media_buy_id.description: Receiver-scoped media buy identifier. On the provider-to-orchestrator hop this is the orchestrator's measurement-facing identifier; on the orchestrator-to-seller hop it is the seller-assigned media buy identifier.

package_id.description: Receiver-scoped package identifier when the assertion is package-specific. The orchestrator maps its measurement-facing identifier to seller-local identifiers during fan-out.

creative_id.description: Receiver-scoped creative identifier when the assertion is creative-specific. The orchestrator maps its measurement-facing identifier to seller-local identifiers during fan-out.

measurement_period.description: Period whose performance is summarized by this assertion.

performance_index.description: Normalized decision signal. 1.0 equals the named baseline, values below 1.0 underperform it, and values above 1.0 outperform it. For ratio-compatible metrics, producers SHOULD compute observed performance divided by baseline performance.

baseline.description: Expectation represented by performance_index = 1.0. Producers using the compact feedback contract MUST populate this field; it remains optional in the schema so existing 3.x payloads remain valid.

metric.description: Metric this assertion describes. Omit only for holistic feedback that is not attributable to one metric.

metric_type.description: **Deprecated as of this minor.** The legacy free-form metric enum that mixes metrics, verification, and attribution into one list. New implementations SHOULD use `metric` (the discriminated `(scope, metric_id, qualifier)` row shape) and populate `metric_type` with a best-effort string for one-minor backwards compatibility. When both `metric` and `metric_type` are present, consumers MUST use `metric` for dispatch. Removed at the next major. See [docs/measurement/taxonomy](https://docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/measurement/taxonomy) for why the layered shape replaces the flat enum.

producer.description: Brand that produced the analysis. When a measurement provider submits to the buyer's orchestrator gateway, the gateway MUST verify this reference against authenticated caller identity. When the orchestrator forwards the assertion to a seller, this field preserves provider attribution while the orchestrator remains the authoritative caller responsible for the claim.

vendor.description: Deprecated alias for producer, retained for compatibility with previously documented payloads. When both are present, consumers use producer.

feedback_source.description: Legacy categorical source hint. Orchestrator-authenticated caller identity and producer attribution provide stronger provenance; retained for compatibility.

methodology.description: Producer-scoped methodology identifier such as geo_incrementality, media_mix_model, or deterministic_attribution. This is intentionally an open string: AdCP does not impose a universal methodology taxonomy.

methodology_version.description: Producer-defined version of the methodology used for this assertion.

study_ref.description: Opaque producer-assigned study or model-run reference. Sellers use it for correlation only and MUST NOT interpret it as an experiment-execution instruction.

evidence.description: Small inline evidence summary used to weight the assertion without transporting the full study.

sample_size.description: Number of observations used for the estimate when the producer can disclose it.

confidence_interval.description: Confidence interval on the performance_index scale.

evidence_ref.description: Provider-hosted evidence or result reference for parties authorized to inspect the full study. The referenced resource remains under the provider's access controls.

as_of.description: When the producer computed this assertion. Useful for historical backfills and model reruns.

final.description: Whether the producer expects this assertion to be revised as data matures. Absence means unspecified.

supersedes_feedback_id.description: Receiver-issued feedback_id of the earlier assertion this one replaces at the same hop. Revisions are new immutable assertions rather than mutations.
